display.title: Teshuvah and Mitzvos: How Every Mitzvah Connects Us to Hashem
display.summary_short: In the Ten Days of Teshuvah, Uncle Yossi explains that a mitzvah connects us to Hashem while an aveirah moves us away, so now is the time to add mitzvos with joy.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, broadcast in the Ten Days of Teshuvah. Uncle Yossi explains that teshuvah means returning to Hashem, and the way back is through mitzvos. Besides 'commandment', the word mitzvah means 'connection': each mitzvah binds us to Hashem. An aveirah does the opposite; the word comes from 'passing over', moving away from Hashem to what is harmful. So in these days we add Torah learning, davening and tzedakah, given straight to a poor person or into a pushka, and we take care to be respectful and honest. The new year, 5747, should be a year full of mitzvos. Quoting Dovid HaMelech, the mitzvos of Hashem are straight and make the heart glad, and there is no greater joy than the joy of a mitzvah.
display.lesson: Every mitzvah brings us closer to Hashem and fills us with joy, so the Ten Days of Teshuvah are the time to add as many mitzvos as we can.
